results.content: Probabilistic record linkage often involves using machine learning algorithms to classify and identify matches automatically. This could potentially be a false positive, where the record linkage process has identified a match that is not actually correct. To evaluate the performance of the record linkage process, it is important to measure precision and recall at different thresholds to see how well it is able to identify true matches and avoid false positives. The figure below shows how the record linkage process was able to identify two matching instances, even though the address field was not an exact match. This demonstrates how the record linkage process was able to take into account other factors, such as the similarity of the names and the phonetic values of the addresses, to identify likely matches. I also discussed phonetic techniques for record linkage data preprocessing and introduced different types of indices that can be used to improve the performance of the record linkage process.

# Data Matching. Concepts and Techniques for Record Linkage, Entity Resolution, and Duplicate Detection. ## Overview. School of Computer Science, The Australian National University, Canberra, Australia. Part of the book series:. Data-Centric Systems and Applications (DCSA). This is a preview of subscription content, log in via an institution. ## Access this book. ## About this book. Data matching (also known as record or data linkage, entity resolution, object identification, or field matching) is the task of identifying, matching and merging records that correspond to the same entities from several databases or even within one database. Based on research in various domains including applied statistics, health informatics, data mining, machine learning, artificial intelligence, database management, and digital libraries, significant advances have been achieved over the last decade in all aspects of the data matching process, especially on how to improve the accuracy of data matching, and its scalability to large databases. Peter Christen’s book is divided into three parts: Part I, “Overview”, introduces the subject by presenting several sample applications and their special challenges, as well as a general overview of a generic data matching process. Part II, “Steps of the Data Matching Process”, then details its main steps like pre-processing, indexing, field and record comparison, classification, and quality evaluation. Lastly, part III, “Further Topics”, deals with specific aspects like privacy, real-time matching, or matching unstructured data. ### Similar content being viewed by others. ## Table of contents (10 chapters). #### The Data Matching Process. ### Steps of the Data Matching Process. #### Data Pre-Processing. ### Further Topics. #### Privacy Aspects of Data Matching. #### Data Matching Systems. ## Authors and Affiliations. ### School of Computer Science, The Australian National University, Canberra, Australia. ## About the author. ## Accessibility Information.
